=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped tightly at the shoot apex, forming a rosette-like arrangement)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or lobes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broad and curved)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off to sides)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, closely spaced, numerous (prominent and forming a reticulate pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, barely visible, leaves appear sessile or nearly so)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is thick, dark, and firm, consistent with young woody growth)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: dark green to brownish (stem appears dark green with some brownish tones, especially near base)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth, no ridges or visible lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipule structures visible at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible upon inspection)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base, not indicative of Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling from various angles. Leaves exhibit minor damage (holes present) but overall morphology is clear. The rosette-like, whorled arrangement of simple, elliptic leaves with pinnate venation and shiny surface is consistent across views. The stem is short, dark, and woody. No reproductive structures or flowers are visible. The seedling is growing on forest floor litter, adjacent to a moss-covered log, but habitat inferences are not made per rules.
